Exploring the MUST-DRIVE Roads in Xinjiang: Where Every Turn Changes the Season | WALKIN XINJIANG·Road. Want a road trip that changes with every curve? Welcome to Xinjiang.
 
 With over 230,000 km of highway – enough to circle half the globe – this isn’t just driving. It’s like turning the pages of a living landscape photo book. One minute you’re cruising past snow-capped peaks, the next you’re rolling through lavender fields so vast they touch the horizon.
 
 We took on Asia’s most epic drives:
 Yizhao Highway, open just 100 days a year, where each bend shifts the season
 Panlong Valley Road, a winding green tunnel through forests straight from a fairytale
 Duku Highway, where deserts, canyons and meadows unfold outside your window
 Then we cranked it up a gear – riding shotgun in a Dakar Rally truck, drifting over golden dunes where the only rule is the thrill of the drive.
 
 Xinjiang doesn’t just have roads. It has routes that rewrite what a road trip can be.

Exploring the MUST-DRIVE Roads in Xinjiang: Where Every Turn Changes the Season | WALKIN XINJIANG·Road. Want a road trip that changes with every curve? Welcome to Xinjiang.
 
 With over 230,000 km of highway – enough to circle half the globe – this isn’t just driving. It’s like turning the pages of a living landscape photo book. One minute you’re cruising past snow-capped peaks, the next you’re rolling through lavender fields so vast they touch the horizon.
 
 We took on Asia’s most epic drives:
 Yizhao Highway, open just 100 days a year, where each bend shifts the season
 Panlong Valley Road, a winding green tunnel through forests straight from a fairytale
 Duku Highway, where deserts, canyons and meadows unfold outside your window
 Then we cranked it up a gear – riding shotgun in a Dakar Rally truck, drifting over golden dunes where the only rule is the thrill of the drive.
 
 Xinjiang doesn’t just have roads. It has routes that rewrite what a road trip can be.

ad_a_text: I’m blind: is the ballet accessible to me? 🩰  Ad✨  Come with me to find out! 💃  I’m so excited that the Royal Ballet and Opera have introduced audio described performances! 🎭 We watched Alice in Wonderland and even got to go ON stage and look at the props and costumes as part of a Touch Tour! 🎟️  It really helped me appreciate the intricacy and detail that goes into every set, and being able to see it up close truly brought the story to life for me! ♥️   Listening to the live audio description; I felt the dancers dominating space with powerful grace.  Every movement poised between strength and softness, control and fluidity.  Its majesty in motion: as their bodies rise, fold and soar in silent dialogue, perfectly in unison with the commanding presence of the orchestra.  It truly is a multisensory experience. 🧡 Have you ever been to the ballet? What did you watch? 💜 Video description: Sassy outside of the Royal Opera house does a delicate spin in a long pink dress. She and Grant clink champagne flutes together. Sassy stands at the stage doors inviting you to come in. A panning sweep of the entire stage, an auditorium can be seen, different sets and Sassy touching the props. She shows you her audio description headset and describes what it looks like. More footage of the costumes, props and sets. Sassy talks about the arabesque she attempts to enact the same grace and poise… more panning shots, and a final shot of the entire cast on stage at the end of the show. #ballett #thingstodoinlondon #london #royalballet #blind #accessibledaysout

ad_b_text: Cake Decorating 101 | Part 4 of 10 This cake is all about colour and getting the little ones involved 🥰 We used the iconic Smarties (for obvious nostalgic reasons). It's super easy to work with, and make decorating a breeze (parents, you’re welcome). This is the kind of cake where kids can jump in, sprinkle freely, arrange the patterns, and proudly say, “I made this.” 💛 #cakedecorating #BirthdayCakeIdeas #FoodiesofSACakeDecoratingSeries #NestleChocolates #NestleSmarties  TOTAL TIME: 1 HR 15 MINS PREP-TIME: 15 MINS COOK TIME: 1 HOUR LEVEL: EASY INGREDIENTS 2 boxes (600g each) vanilla flavoured cake mix (and all ingredients required for the box mix) 6 boxes (40g each) Nestlé Smarties Chocolate 1 tub store-bought chocolate icing METHOD 1. Preheat oven and prepare two 23cm cake pans by spraying with non-stick spray and lining with baking paper. Alternatively bake the mix as cupcakes. 2. Mix the cake batter per the box instructions. Chop 1 box of Nestlé Smarties Chocolate and gently fold it into the cake batter. Pour the batter into the prepared cake pans or cupcake papers and bake. Allow to cool completely on a wire rack, then refrigerate until firm, approximately 1 hour. 3. Take a small cutter or object, like a mug or bowl, to mark a circle in the exact center of both cakes. Using a sharp knife, cut out and remove the center piece from both cakes, leaving you with two large cake rings. *Chef's tip: alternatively use a bundt cake tin 4. Divide each cake ring into four quarters. Remove the top-right quarter from the first ring and the bottom-right quarter from the second ring. 5. Look at the inner edges of the remaining two large 'C' shapes. Trim a very small, crescent-shaped piece off the inner edge of both C-shapes where they will meet in the middle to form the figure-eight. This ensures the two main pieces can touch and join cleanly. 6. Carefully arrange the two large C-shaped pieces onto a serving board, pushing the trimmed edges together in the center to form the number '3'. 7. Apply a thin layer of the store-bought chocolate icing all over the cake to seal any crumbs. Chill for 15 minutes. Then, apply a smooth, thick, and even second layer of icing over the entire surface of the assembled number cake. This acts as the "glue" for the Smarties decoration. 8. Sort the remaining whole Smarties by colour. Starting at the edges, lay the whole Smarties onto the iced cake in neat rows or distinct color lines. Press each Smartie gently into the icing to secure the colourful, patterned finish. Alternatively, arrange the cupcakes in a number 3 shape, ice to join the cupcakes together and decorate with Smarties. 9. Refrigerate the decorated cake for at least 15 minutes to allow the icing to set and the Smarties to adhere firmly. 10. When ready, use a sharp knife to slice and serve this fun, festive Smarties Celebration Confetti Cake, and ENJOY!

ad_a_text: 🧬 Addiction isn’t a choice. It’s a disease. For decades, society has told us that addiction is a matter of willpower - that people should “just stop.” But modern genetics and neuroscience tell a very different story. There are over 270 genes that increase the risk of developing Alcohol Use Disorder. Combine that with trauma, mental health struggles, and constant exposure to alcohol in our culture — and what you get isn’t a lack of discipline. It’s biology. 🧠 Addiction rewires the brain. It shuts down the part responsible for decision-making and future planning. And the cruel irony? Many people who carry these genes can tolerate more alcohol before feeling its effects, which means they often reach dangerous levels without realizing it. We would never shame someone for having diabetes, cancer, or heart disease. Yet when it comes to addiction - another genetic, medical illness - we blame, isolate, and moralize. It’s time for that to change. It’s time for compassion.  If you take one thing from this - let it be this: Addiction is not your fault. But recovery is possible. And it starts with understanding the science. #alcohol #addiction #recovery  #mentalhealth #mentalhealthmatters

ad_b_text: Leftovers never looked this good 😋Turn your holiday turkey into Creamy Poblano Turkey Enchiladas topped with rich, authentic LALA Crema Mexicana. Because when you deck the table with LALA, every bite feels like home. ❤️   #DeckTheTable #LALACremaMexicana #HolidayLeftovers #AuthenticFlavor Recipe ⬇️  Ingredients: 2 tbsps butter 2 poblano peppers, chopped Minced garlic 1/4 cup flour 11/4 cup chicken broth 11/4 cup heavy whipping cream 1 tbsp onion powder 1 tsp salt 1 cup cilantro, diced 2 cups left over turkey 1-4oz cans hatch green chilis, diced 2 cups Colby jack cheese, shredded Corn tortillas Sauce: 1. Place butter into pan on medium heat and let melt. Then add in chopped up poblano peppers to sauté for about 5 min. 2. Once softened add in minced garlic and cook for 2 min. Then add in flour and slow mix together for additional 3 min. 3. Then add in chicken broth and mix well. Once the sauce thickens, transfer it to another bowl and blend together with an immersion blender. (Could also use a regular blender) 4. Transfer sauce back to pan and once it comes to a simmer add in heavy whipping cream, salt, onion powder, cilantro and mix well. Enchiladas Filling: In a bowl mix turkey, Colby jack cheese, and green hatch chilis Assemble Enchiladas and sprinkle shredded cheese on top. Place in the oven at 375 for 15min until cheese is melted. Pro tip: place corn tortillas in microwave wrapped in a towel for about 30 seconds to softened them so they don’t tear when assembling enchiladas.

ad_a_text: Soft & Fluffy Milk Powder Cake – A Sweet Eid Delight! 🍰✨   Celebrate Eid with this Milk Powder Cake – light, airy, and packed with rich, milky flavour! Made with simple pantry staples, it's an easy yet delicious treat to share with family and friends.     Ingredients:   🥛 2 ½ cups East End Milk Powder   🍚 ⅔ cup sugar   🧁 1 tbsp baking powder   🥚 3 eggs   🌿 ¼ cup vegetable oil   🥛 Dashes of milk (as needed), Caramel Sauce or Dulce De Leche  Method: 1️⃣ Toast the milk powder – Lightly toast the milk powder in a pan for a few minutes, making sure to keep stirring to prevent clumping and burning. Remove from the stove. 2️⃣ Combine dry ingredients – mix the toasted milk powder, baking powder, and sugar until well combined.   3️⃣ Whisk wet ingredients – In a separate bowl, beat the eggs, oil, and a dash of milk until smooth.   4️⃣ Mix together – Gradually add the wet mixture into the dry ingredients, stirring until a batter forms. Add more milk if needed to get a better consistency.   5️⃣ Bake – Pour the batter into a greased cake tin and use a spoon to flatten the thick cake batter to fit into the cake tin. Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean.   6️⃣ Let it cool before adding the caramel sauce. Slice then enjoy this soft and fluffy Eid treat!     Would you make this for your Eid celebrations? These Indian-spiced minced meat & peas samosas are the perfect balance of crunch and spice, made effortlessly with East End’s finest spices. ✨ Here’s how to make them: 🌿 Ingredients: • 250g minced lamb • 1 small onion, finely chopped • 1 tsp East End Cumin Seeds • 1 tsp East End Garam Masala • ½ tsp East End Turmeric Powder • 1 tsp East End Coriander Powder • ½ tsp East End Chilli Powder (adjust to taste) • ½ tsp salt • 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste • 50g green peas • 1 tbsp fresh coriander, chopped • 1 tbsp oil • 1 pack of samosa pastry sheets • Water for sealing • Oil for frying 🥄 Method: 1️⃣ Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan, add East End Cumin Seeds, and let them sizzle. Add chopped onions and sauté until golden. 2️⃣ Stir in ginger-garlic paste and minced meat. Cook until browned. 3️⃣ Add East End Garam Masala, Turmeric, Coriander Powder, Chilli Powder, and salt. Mix well. 4️⃣ Stir in green peas and cook for another 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool. Mix in fresh coriander. 5️⃣ Take a samosa pastry sheet, fold into a triangle, and fill with 1-2 tbsp of the mixture. Seal with flour paste. 6️⃣ Deep-fry until crispy and golden. Drain on kitchen paper. Serve hot with East End Green Chilli Sauce or East End Tamarind Sauce!  Who’s ready to try these? 🙌 #samosas #keemasamosa #samosarecipe #homemadesamosa #eastend #garammasala

ad_a_text: It’s #valentinesday with @Australian Eggs! So here’s my #recipefromtheheart - Mini rose Basque cheesecakes with rose cream and rose syrup topping! They’re easy, SO pretty and the perfect way to celebrate love with EVERYONE you care for. #joyfulfood #eggrecipes  RECIPE:  Cheesecake ingredients:  - 500g cream cheese, room temperature - 1 cup thickened cream - ½ cup caster sugar - ½ tsp salt - ½ tsp vanilla extract  - ¼ cup plain flour - 3 eggs - hint of pink food colouring (optional, look for natural) - ½ tsp rose essence  Rose syrup:  - 1 cup caster sugar - 1 cup water - pink food colour - 1 tsp rose water Rose cream topping:  - 1 cup thickened cream - 1 Tbsp caster sugar  - pink food colour  - 1 tsp rose essence  METHOD:  - First make your rose syrup; simmering together the water and caster sugar until dissolved and slightly thickened. - Allow to cool completely, then stir in a drop of two of pink food colouring and 1 tsp rose water. Keep chilled until needed. Keeps for 4 weeks in the fridge and makes a perfect addition to cocktails too! - Pre-heat your oven to 220C (fan forced). And line a cupcake or muffin tin with baking papers or patty cases for 18 mini cheesecakes — you can do batches.   In a stand mixer with a paddle or with electric beaters, whip the cream cheese until smooth. Add in the cream and mix lightly. Then add the sugar, salt, and vanilla extract, beating until you cannot feel any sugar granules when you rub the mix between your fingers.  - Sprinkle the flour over the batter and mix in the eggs one at a time, beating lightly after each addition to incorporate, then add the rose essence and mix, before swirling in a little pink food colour.  - Pour the batter into the prepared tin and bake on the middle shelf for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheesecakes look almost burnt on the outside, this is the signature caramelisation.  - Allow to cool completely, or chill in the fridge.  - Meanwhile, whip the cream, caster sugar and rose essence and swirl in a few drops of pink food colouring.  - To serve, top each mini cheesecake with a swirl of rose cream, a scattering of rose petals, pistachio and fairy floss and a drizzle of rose syrup.

ad_b_text: You had us at Peanut Butter Ice Cream 😍! Learn how @zee_thecook puts together these chilled sensations with YUM YUM. Try the recipe below: Ingredients: 3 1⁄2 packets Oreo biscuits, about 49 cookies 500g fresh cream 1 tbsp. YUM YUM peanut butter 150g condensed milk 2 knobs Melted butter 6 pieces chocolate chopped Method: 1. Line a square baking dish with parchment paper. 2. Add the Oreos to a zip lock bag and smack them with a rolling pin until finely crushed. 3. In a bowl add crushed biscuits with melted butter, mix together until a crumbly mixture is formed. 4. Pour half of the Oreo mixture into the square dish, spread evenly and press down using the glass. 5. Place the pan into the freezer while you prepare the ice cream. In a separate bowl: 1. Use an electric hand mixer to beat heavy cream until it becomes stiff peaks, add in YUM YUM peanut butter and whisk again. 2. Slowly pour the condensed milk, crushed biscuits and chocolate and fold together until combined. 3. Remove the square dish from the freeze and pour the ice cream mixture onto the crust and spread out evenly. 4. Freeze for 3 hours. 5. Add the remaining Oreo crumbs on top of the ice cream mixture, use the glass to press the mixture very gently so it sticks. 6. Freeze over night. 7. Cut into squares. Enjoy!!!! #YUMYUMGoesNutsInSummer

ad_a_text: It’s #valentinesday with @Australian Eggs! So here’s my #recipefromtheheart - Mini rose Basque cheesecakes with rose cream and rose syrup topping! They’re easy, SO pretty and the perfect way to celebrate love with EVERYONE you care for. #joyfulfood #eggrecipes  RECIPE:  Cheesecake ingredients:  - 500g cream cheese, room temperature - 1 cup thickened cream - ½ cup caster sugar - ½ tsp salt - ½ tsp vanilla extract  - ¼ cup plain flour - 3 eggs - hint of pink food colouring (optional, look for natural) - ½ tsp rose essence  Rose syrup:  - 1 cup caster sugar - 1 cup water - pink food colour - 1 tsp rose water Rose cream topping:  - 1 cup thickened cream - 1 Tbsp caster sugar  - pink food colour  - 1 tsp rose essence  METHOD:  - First make your rose syrup; simmering together the water and caster sugar until dissolved and slightly thickened. - Allow to cool completely, then stir in a drop of two of pink food colouring and 1 tsp rose water. Keep chilled until needed. Keeps for 4 weeks in the fridge and makes a perfect addition to cocktails too! - Pre-heat your oven to 220C (fan forced). And line a cupcake or muffin tin with baking papers or patty cases for 18 mini cheesecakes — you can do batches.   In a stand mixer with a paddle or with electric beaters, whip the cream cheese until smooth. Add in the cream and mix lightly. Then add the sugar, salt, and vanilla extract, beating until you cannot feel any sugar granules when you rub the mix between your fingers.  - Sprinkle the flour over the batter and mix in the eggs one at a time, beating lightly after each addition to incorporate, then add the rose essence and mix, before swirling in a little pink food colour.  - Pour the batter into the prepared tin and bake on the middle shelf for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheesecakes look almost burnt on the outside, this is the signature caramelisation.  - Allow to cool completely, or chill in the fridge.  - Meanwhile, whip the cream, caster sugar and rose essence and swirl in a few drops of pink food colouring.  - To serve, top each mini cheesecake with a swirl of rose cream, a scattering of rose petals, pistachio and fairy floss and a drizzle of rose syrup.

ad_b_text: You had us at Peanut Butter Ice Cream 😍! Learn how @zee_thecook puts together these chilled sensations with YUM YUM. Try the recipe below: Ingredients: 3 1⁄2 packets Oreo biscuits, about 49 cookies 500g fresh cream 1 tbsp. YUM YUM peanut butter 150g condensed milk 2 knobs Melted butter 6 pieces chocolate chopped Method: 1. Line a square baking dish with parchment paper. 2. Add the Oreos to a zip lock bag and smack them with a rolling pin until finely crushed. 3. In a bowl add crushed biscuits with melted butter, mix together until a crumbly mixture is formed. 4. Pour half of the Oreo mixture into the square dish, spread evenly and press down using the glass. 5. Place the pan into the freezer while you prepare the ice cream. In a separate bowl: 1. Use an electric hand mixer to beat heavy cream until it becomes stiff peaks, add in YUM YUM peanut butter and whisk again. 2. Slowly pour the condensed milk, crushed biscuits and chocolate and fold together until combined. 3. Remove the square dish from the freeze and pour the ice cream mixture onto the crust and spread out evenly. 4. Freeze for 3 hours. 5. Add the remaining Oreo crumbs on top of the ice cream mixture, use the glass to press the mixture very gently so it sticks. 6. Freeze over night. 7. Cut into squares. Enjoy!!!! #YUMYUMGoesNutsInSummer
